novels.title: The Wrong Heiress: The Girl They Disowned Was the Heir to the World's Greatest Dynasty
novels.subtitle: The Wrong Heiress
novels.synopsis:
Aria Sterling had everything a wealthy young woman could want.

A luxurious mansion, an influential family, expensive education, and a future secured by one of the most prestigious business dynasties in the country.

At least, that was what she believed.

Everything changed when a shocking revelation exposed a hospital identity switch: Aria was not biologically related to the Sterling family. Their real daughter, Victoria, had finally been found.

For the Sterling family, the decision was obvious.

Their biological daughter would reclaim her rightful position.

Aria, the girl they had raised for twenty years, was now an unwanted reminder of a mistake.

Victoria returned to her biological family with grand expectations. She wanted recognition, admiration, luxury, and the unquestionable position she believed belonged to her.

Aria, meanwhile, simply wanted to leave peacefully and start over.

Neither girl knew the truth.

The discarded daughter was the missing successor of the Vesper Sovereign Dynasty, an extraordinarily powerful family whose influence extended across international finance, industry, technology, intelligence, political relationships, and the criminal underworld.

For years, the dynasty had searched for its missing heir.

Its patriarch had refused to appoint a permanent successor. Its corporate leaders had prepared for her return. Its intelligence organization had investigated countless leads. Its international allies had been waiting for the person whose authority could unite their interests.

And now, they had finally found her.

Unfortunately, their long-awaited heiress had absolutely no idea who they were.

As Aria attempts to live an ordinary life, the world's most influential people begin converging around her. Corporate chairmen become nervous, international power brokers reconsider their decisions, and the criminal underworld prepares to welcome its most unexpected authority.

Meanwhile, Victoria is convinced that Aria is somehow stealing the life that rightfully belongs to her.

But the greatest problem facing the Vesper Dynasty isn't its rivals, its enemies, or its succession crisis.

It is convincing their missing heiress that they are, in fact, her family.
